amendments.rule: Where the ASV compresses a negator with the duration phrase `εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` into the single negation *never*, that one English word stays whole on the negator and every token of the duration phrase is its own `unrepresented` unit. Where the negator is `οὐ μή`, rule 33 keeps the word on the particle pair: `οὐ μὴ ἀπόλωνται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *shall never perish*, `οὐ μὴ διψήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *shall never thirst*, and `οὐ μὴ θεωρήσῃ θάνατον εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *shall never see death* leave the preposition, the article and the noun empty, because the single English word answers to the negation and nothing is left over for them. A **plain** negator does the same and is its own `aligned` unit headed on *never*, the particle pair being no part of what licenses this: `οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *hath never forgiveness* gives *never* to `οὐκ` and leaves `εἰς`, `τόν` and `αἰῶνα` empty. What decides it is that one English word carries the negation and the duration together, not which negator the Greek wrote. Rule 30 is the contrast and the ASV's phrasing decides it: where the ASV writes *for ever* the ordinary analysis applies, `εἰς` taking *for* and `αἰῶνα` taking *ever*, as `ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *shall live for ever* and `ὁ υἱὸς μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *the son abideth for ever* do. John 8 does both in one chapter, so this is rule 24's habit and not two analyses. Do not stretch *never* over the phrase, do not split it away from the negator in order to give the noun a word, and do not reach for `noncompositional` over the whole clause. A reference comparison will report all three duration tokens as disagreements, and that report is not a correction.
amendments.why: MRK.3.29 `οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα` → *hath never forgiveness* is exactly the case rule 48 gives its reasoning for — one English word carrying negation and duration, nothing left over for the preposition, article and noun — but the rule's text scopes that reasoning to `οὐ μή`, so the verse pass had to apply it by analogy and say so in four notes. The pair is doing no work in the argument: rule 33 is cited only to keep the word whole across two particles, and a single negator needs no such help. Returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because a new one would leave rule 48's `οὐ μή`-only sentence standing for whoever reads it first, which is the exact failure the brief names. The widening is narrow, contradicts nothing in the corpus shown, and covers a recurring synoptic idiom rather than a shape peculiar to this chapter.

conventions: A supplied English preposition that marks a verb's own bare object rides with the governed word and not with the verb, whatever the object's case. MRK.3.5 περιβλεψάμενος αὐτούς → *looked round about* / *on them*, MRK.3.9 προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ → *wait* / *on him*, MRK.3.10 ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ → *pressed* / *upon him*, MRK.3.11 προσέπιπτον αὐτῷ → *fell down* / *before him*, MRK.3.21 κρατῆσαι αὐτόν → *to lay hold* / *on him*, MRK.3.32 ζητοῦσίν σε → *seek* / *for thee*, and MRK.3.34 τούς → *on them*. Rule 106's closing clause names a bare dative or genitive; this chapter extends it to an accusative object the ASV writes with a supplied preposition, so *lay hold on* and *seek for* are not read as phrasal verbs. A preverb particle that governs nothing — *out*, *up*, *forth*, *together*, *round*, *down* — still rides inside the verb's own unit under rule 106's main clause, which is why 3.10 leaves ἐπιπίπτειν only *pressed* while 3.13 keeps *up* on ἀναβαίνει.

No supplied English *and* in this chapter is `added`. Rule 88 places the juncture of a participle-to-coordinate conversion on the verb it introduces at MRK.3.6 (ἐδίδουν → *and took*), MRK.3.23 (ἔλεγεν → *and said*) and MRK.3.33 (λέγει → *and saith*), and MRK.3.27's εἰσελθὼν … διαρπάσαι → *enter … and spoil* is read the same way, the circumstantial participle being the token that licenses the word. Rule 98's `added` seam is scoped in terms to an asyndetic seam between two **like** constituents both rendered alike, and a participle converted into a coordinate infinitive clause is not that seam.

ἐπιτίθημι with ὄνομα rendered by the single English verb *surnamed* is one rule 73 unit with the **source** head on the finite verb rather than on the noun, at MRK.3.16 (ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα) and MRK.3.17 (ἐπέθηκεν ὀνόματα). Rule 10 leaves the source head of a multi-source unit open and the corpus takes this construction both ways; both instances here read it the same, and the noun remains the defensible alternative.

report: Checked all 48 candidate lemma groups and read the whole dump end to end, because the candidate table is blind to `added` units. This chapter has exactly one such unit — the rule 37 versification unit at MRK.3.19 — and its counterpart tokens are `unrepresented` at MRK.3.20 with a matching note, so both sides say so and neither reaches across. No hidden added/fold split.

No genuine cross-verse split found. Every multi-treatment group is licensed by the source or by the English the ASV wrote: ὁ empties under rule 20 where a genitive pronoun stands (3.5, 3.7, 3.9, 3.27, 3.31–3.34) and takes the supplied possessive where none does (3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.28), which is rule 20's two arms; οὐ δύναται joins as *cannot* at 3.24 and 3.26 and splits at 3.25 where the ASV writes *will not be able*; ἵνα μή is `noncompositional` as *lest* at 3.9 and splits as *that … not* at 3.12, rule 39's test in both directions; ὅτι is recitative and empty at 3.11, 3.21, 3.22 (twice) and 3.28 and causal *because* at 3.30; ἐάν is conditional *if* at 3.24–3.25 and the separately written *soever* at 3.28 under rules 50 and 72.

Rule 106 is applied uniformly: a preverb particle governing nothing (*out*, *up*, *forth*, *together*, *round*, *down*) stays inside its verb's unit at 3.5, 3.6, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15, 3.20, 3.21, 3.22, 3.23, 3.26 and 3.34, and an expressed preposition whose own gloss carries the particle takes the whole prepositional expression (εἰς → *into* at 3.1, 3.13, 3.27). περιβλεψάμενος keeps *round about* at 3.5 but only *round* at 3.34, because περὶ αὐτὸν κύκλῳ stands there and takes *about* and its own *round* — a source-licensed difference, not a split.

The supplied English preposition marking a verb's bare object goes to the governed word in all seven instances regardless of case: dative at 3.9, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.34, accusative at 3.5, 3.21 and 3.32. Rule 106's closing clause names only a bare dative or genitive, so the accusative cases are a chapter judgment and are recorded as a convention rather than promoted, the phrasal reading of *lay hold on* and *seek for* being defensible and the corpus not consulted on it.

No supplied English *and* is `added` anywhere in the chapter: rule 88 puts the participle-to-coordinate juncture on the verb it introduces at 3.6, 3.23 and 3.33, and 3.27's εἰσελθὼν … διαρπάσαι → *enter … and spoil* reads the same way. Rule 98's `added` seam is scoped to two like constituents both rendered alike and does not reach a participle converted into a coordinate infinitive clause. Recorded as a convention because it decides a status.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. Ten of the fourteen are the documented article convention (τό at 3.3 under rule 93; τῆς and ἡ at 3.5, ἡ at 3.24 and 3.25 under rules 20 and 38; τοῦ at 3.17 and οἱ at 3.22 under rules 23 and 31). παρ at 3.21 is rule 36's possessive compression in οἱ παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ → *his friends*. The three MRK.3.20 tokens are the rule 37 versification the report already says is not a correction. The three MRK.3.29 duration tokens are the *never* compression, which the amendment below settles. Nothing was changed to improve the aggregate.

One amendment returned: rule 48 is widened to a plain negator, MRK.3.29 οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα → *hath never forgiveness* having met the case rule 48 states its reasoning for but scopes to οὐ μή. No new rules: the object-preposition and juncture judgments are logged as conventions instead.
